9NS86BQ33SPX:couch.text: A cheerful open-world sandbox where you take silly jobs, do mini games and wander a colourful town together on split-screen. The exploring and low-pressure goofing around echo LEGO games and Stardew's earn-and-spend loop.
9NS86BQ33SPX:couch.caveat: It's more of a loose sandbox than a guided story, so it may feel aimless without the puzzle and mystery structure they like.

9NXVC0482QS5:couch.text: A two-player split-screen adventure where you and Tay swap between platforming, puzzles and goofy set pieces, each with different roles. It sits close to A Way Out and It Takes Two-style teamwork, with a cute, funny tone.
9NXVC0482QS5:couch.caveat: Some sections lean on timing and action, and the difficulty can't be adjusted, so Tay may find a few parts stressful.

C4VKLMG1HLZW:couch.text: Two yarn creatures swing, climb and pull each other through gentle platforming puzzles in pretty, colourful landscapes. The cooperation is the core, which suits a shared-screen pair who enjoy It Takes Two.
C4VKLMG1HLZW:couch.caveat: Some stages need precise jumping and timing, and the co-op can get fiddly when one player lags behind.

C042M8GWKS34:couch.text: You hop into larger and smaller nesting dolls and use each one's special ability to solve quirky puzzles with a humorous, storybook feel. Puzzles can be tackled in different ways, so there's little pressure.
C042M8GWKS34:couch.caveat: The co-op listing is flagged as conflicting, so confirm two-player local play really works before committing.

9NMB4T25W817:couch.text: A silly open-world sandbox where you wander as goats, wreck things with physics and chase daft objectives together. It's colorful and low-pressure, with exploring and messing about like the LEGO games.
9NMB4T25W817:couch.caveat: It's more about random chaos than structured puzzles or story, so it may wear thin after a while.

BSMZH25V6V46:couch.text: A physics-based puzzle-adventure where two players control wobbly characters, pushing, climbing and carrying things to get through open, explorable levels. The silly, forgiving feel and shared problem-solving echo LEGO games and It Takes Two.
BSMZH25V6V46:couch.caveat: The floppy, imprecise controls can be frustrating, and getting stuck on a physics puzzle may test Tay's patience.

9PC4RWP34M2D:couch.text: You place wobbly units on a battlefield and watch them fight in a physics-driven comedy. The humour is the draw, and the split-screen mode is versus rather than co-op.
9PC4RWP34M2D:couch.caveat: The local mode is head-to-head, not co-op, and it's a strategy sim with little puzzle or adventure.

9P88K6NQW12H:couch.text: You and Tay haul furniture and awkward items through houses and odd levels, coordinating throws and carries. It's silly, colourful and has an easygoing teamwork feel similar to the LEGO games.
9P88K6NQW12H:couch.caveat: Later levels can get chaotic and time-pressured, which may stress Tay.

9NZG72SH3H4W:couch.text: You load up vehicles and deliver parcels around a wobbly open world, with physics making every trip a joke. Exploring and goofing around together fits the light LEGO-style mood.
9NZG72SH3H4W:couch.caveat: Controls are deliberately floppy and reviews are middling, so it may feel clumsy rather than charming.

9P743P6195Q5:couch.text: A direct follow-up to a game they already like: you and a partner work through themed escape rooms on a shared split-screen, hunting for clues and solving puzzles together, with a campus conspiracy mystery running underneath.
9P743P6195Q5:couch.caveat: Some puzzle rooms may get tricky or time-pressured for Tay, and there's no adjustable difficulty to ease things off.

9NR7XDNVP5SW:couch.text: An interactive drama where you make story choices together, with mystery and an emotional, adult storyline. It's close to A Way Out in its story-first approach and needs only simple controls.
9NR7XDNVP5SW:couch.caveat: It has dark themes and tense moments, and it's mostly choosing options rather than puzzles, so it may be heavier than they want.

BQ9Q620NC614:couch.text: A fairy-tale adventure with hand-painted art, where one player guides the heroine and the other controls a small companion. Turn-based battles and light exploration keep it gentle.
BQ9Q620NC614:couch.caveat: The second player has a limited role, and the turn-based RPG combat may feel slow or fiddly for a co-op pair.

9N6Z8DQXSQWH:couch.text: You wander Disneyland together, meeting characters and doing small quests tied to the attractions. It's easygoing and exploratory, which fits the relaxed side of their tastes.
9N6Z8DQXSQWH:couch.caveat: It's aimed at younger kids, so the quests are simple and may feel shallow.

BTBWBGKPKS97:couch.text: A dark-humoured puzzle platformer where a team of adventurers explores a talking cave, each with a special ability. Puzzles need cooperation and the tone is wry rather than frightening.
BTBWBGKPKS97:couch.caveat: It's built for three players, so two will have to handle a character each plus an AI one, and it involves some backtracking.

9PLF73SS7M6J:couch.text: A collection of Rabbids mini-games with some puzzle and adventure elements, all silly and family-friendly. Easy to pick up for a short evening.
9PLF73SS7M6J:couch.caveat: Mini-game compilations tend to be shallow and lack the story and puzzle depth they enjoy.

C26K4DVGR45B:couch.text: A colorful, funny platformer where you run, jump and slap your way through levels side by side. The cartoon look and shared-screen co-op suit the LEGO-style fun you both like.
C26K4DVGR45B:couch.caveat: It's a precise platformer with rhythm-based levels and bosses, which could be too high-skill for Tay.

BWVBNCMF22ZK:couch.text: A short, story-driven prison-escape adventure played entirely in split-screen, with each of you controlling one of the two prisoners. You already like it, so it's a natural one to replay or finish together.
BWVBNCMF22ZK:couch.caveat: If you've already played it, there's little new, and it has some tense action and shooting sections.

9NFQ1XMXDLN6:couch.text: A bright, simple platformer where two players explore themed worlds and do mini-games with Gabby's cats. Very easy to pick up.
9NFQ1XMXDLN6:couch.caveat: It's made for young children, so it may feel too simple and repetitive for two adults.

C3B1V55CDL0C:couch.text: A free platform fighter with plenty of characters, local play for up to eight, and a family-friendly cartoon look. It could work as a casual party game.
C3B1V55CDL0C:couch.caveat: It's competitive fighting that rewards skill and practice, which runs against Tay's dislike of high-skill games.

9NJWFF2KHL6H:couch.text: A 3D platformer in which you explore a cartoon Europe as Ben 10, switching aliens to solve puzzles and fight. Two-player split-screen keeps it LEGO-like.
9NJWFF2KHL6H:couch.caveat: Combat is a big part of it, and review scores are middling.

C2WKJJ9F5936:couch.text: A fantasy open-world action RPG where you explore Albion, take quests and use melee, ranged and magic attacks. It has an exploration and adventure feel, with a second player who can join in.
C2WKJJ9F5936:couch.caveat: Co-op is limited, the game is old, and the combat and RPG systems may be more involved than Tay would like.

9N8NJ74FZTG9:couch.text: A colourful, Minecraft-style dungeon crawler where you fight through levels and collect loot together on one TV. It's easy to pick up and cute.
9N8NJ74FZTG9:couch.caveat: Combat is the whole game and gets hectic, which may not suit Tay.

BVJLKDG2TX8H:couch.text: You and Tay run a chaotic kitchen, chopping, cooking and passing dishes while the layout shifts around you. The cute, funny tone and teamwork fit your tastes.
BVJLKDG2TX8H:couch.caveat: It's flagged as difficult, and the time pressure and shouting at each other can feel stressful, which Tay dislikes.

BR46KM4D5B9L:couch.text: An action RPG with a humorous tone, an open world to explore and a story about leading a kingdom, with a second player able to join.
BR46KM4D5B9L:couch.caveat: Combat-heavy and menu-driven, with less puzzle and mystery than they usually look for.

9N79TQTZTQQ4:couch.text: A pixel-art Marvel beat 'em up with short levels and simple controls, playable by up to four on one TV.
9N79TQTZTQQ4:couch.caveat: It's wall-to-wall fighting with no puzzles or exploration, which cuts against what they enjoy.

9NQVHHW88XW9:couch.text: A gentle, family-friendly puzzle-adventure set in Bluey's world, where you explore and solve light puzzles together on one screen. It's low-pressure and easy to pick up, in the same spirit as the LEGO games.
9NQVHHW88XW9:couch.caveat: It's aimed at young children, so the puzzles may feel too simple and short for two adults.

BWT2GPVWCH2F:couch.text: A calm, pixel-art kingdom builder where you ride across the land, collect coins, recruit subjects and build walls together. The slow pace and exploration are a bit like Stardew Valley.
BWT2GPVWCH2F:couch.caveat: It's quite slow and repetitive, and the nightly enemy attacks can create some tension.

BX27S00SKW1V:couch.text: A funny, colourful 3D platformer full of collecting and exploring, in the same spirit as the LEGO games. The split-screen mode is the catch for your profile.
BX27S00SKW1V:couch.caveat: The two-player part is versus minigames, not co-op through the adventure. The main game is single-player, and its camera and platforming can be fiddly.

BQRB60PW2SDL:couch.text: A kart racer with cartoon characters, tracks and power-ups, which you can play on a split screen together. The controls are simple and the tone is silly.
BQRB60PW2SDL:couch.caveat: It's competitive and racing skill matters, so it's not a puzzle or adventure game, and it may feel stressful for Tay.

9P8XKV2D5DZ5:couch.text: You dig underground for resources, then hurry back to defend your dome from alien waves, and split-screen lets two people share the job. There is a nice exploration and upgrade loop, and it suits a team of two.
9P8XKV2D5DZ5:couch.caveat: The timed waves and dark atmosphere add pressure, and the roguelike runs can be hard, which may stress Tay.

9P88K6NQW12H:party.text: You and up to three friends haul furniture through physics-driven levels, throwing sofas through windows and into a van. It's the same silly, shared-chaos feel as Boomerang Fu, with a cooperative goal and simple controls anyone can pick up.
9P88K6NQW12H:party.caveat: It's capped at 4 players and co-operative, so bigger groups will have to rotate and there's no head-to-head element.

BVJLKDG2TX8H:party.text: You and up to three friends run a kitchen together, shouting orders as you chop, cook and plate against the clock. It's quick to explain and gets loud and funny, much like the chaos you enjoy in Boomerang Fu.
BVJLKDG2TX8H:party.caveat: It caps at four players, so a bigger group will have people waiting for a turn.

BQRB60PW2SDL:party.text: A kart racer with split-screen for up to four, where you drift, grab weapons and hit rivals. Races are short and easy to pick up, and there are also battle arenas for some head-to-head mayhem.
BQRB60PW2SDL:party.caveat: Four-player split-screen limits bigger groups, and the drift and boost mechanics take a few races to get comfortable with.

9NMB4T25W817:party.text: You and up to three friends wreck a physics-driven sandbox as goats, with mini-games to compete in or just break things together. It leans on the same silly physics comedy as Ultimate Chicken Horse.
9NMB4T25W817:party.caveat: It's mostly a loose sandbox without much structure, so a group may run out of things to do together fairly quickly.

9PMX3SK2RMG4:party.text: Each round is a different absurd dodgeball variant, so you're throwing balls at friends in short, funny matches. It joins the sports side of your tastes with party-game chaos, and up to four can play on one console.
9PMX3SK2RMG4:party.caveat: It's limited to 4 players, and since it's newer and little reviewed, I can't say how deep or varied the modes get.

C22T53SQ7FLM:party.text: A collection of 30 Rare games, including some with local multiplayer, so you can pick something short and silly for a night. It's more of a grab-bag to dip into than one dedicated party game.
C22T53SQ7FLM:party.caveat: Only a handful of the games are actually good couch multiplayer, and many are older titles with dated controls.

9PN0LC4CNLPT:party.text: A platform fighter where cartoon characters knock each other off the stage, with up to four on one console. It's close to Gang Beasts and Boomerang Fu in being a quick free-for-all, though the controls are more technical.
9PN0LC4CNLPT:party.caveat: Platform fighters reward learning each character's moves, so newcomers may get beaten by anyone who has practiced, and it's capped at 4.

9NZG72SH3H4W:party.text: You drive a delivery truck and carry parcels around an open sandbox with up to three friends on one screen, with floppy physics making every handoff go wrong. That wobbly, funny chaos is close to Gang Beasts and Ultimate Chicken Horse.
9NZG72SH3H4W:party.caveat: It tops out at four players, so a bigger couch crowd will have to rotate in, and the critic score is middling, so the novelty may fade quickly.

9P1H8K2V0NNP:party.text: Everyone builds the racecourse together by adding obstacles and traps, then races bikes through it. That's the same build-then-sabotage loop as Ultimate Chicken Horse, and the store listing mentions local play with a larger group.
9P1H8K2V0NNP:party.caveat: The player count on one console is disputed in the data, so check that your group of 8 can all play before committing.

9NP6V9LFVJ87:party.text: A baseball game with arcade styling and a relaxed difficulty option that sits between a sports sim and something friendlier. Two can play against each other or up to four can team up on one console.
9NP6V9LFVJ87:party.caveat: Baseball is slow-paced and takes rules knowledge, so it isn't a loud chaotic party game, and the co-op cap is 4.

9P0RGJND5SR0:party.text: A faster, shorter take on Monopoly where players race around a city, buy properties, and mess with each other, with up to six on one console. It's a familiar rule set for a mixed group.
9P0RGJND5SR0:party.caveat: Steam reviews are poor at 43% positive, and it may feel more like a board game than the quick chaotic action you prefer.

C26K4DVGR45B:party.text: A colorful platformer where up to four friends run, jump and slap through levels side by side. The pace is fast, the levels are short, and the shared platforming is similar in spirit to Lovers in a Dangerous Spacetime.
C26K4DVGR45B:party.caveat: It's co-operative rather than competitive and tops out at four players, so a bigger or more rivalry-minded group may find it tame.

9N93V5M3TG4N:party.text: A baseball game with arcade styling, local play, and up to four on one console. It covers the sports side of your tastes, with simple controls and accessible matches for a mixed group.
9N93V5M3TG4N:party.caveat: Baseball is slow-paced and rules-heavy for a chaotic party night, and it's limited to 4 players.

BP6V6QZBMFP0:party.text: Physics-driven motorbike stunts where you race through obstacle courses, with local play for up to four. The wobbly physics are funny to watch, and it mixes the competitiveness of sports with the chaos of Chicken Horse.
BP6V6QZBMFP0:party.caveat: It's tagged as difficult and the controls take practice, with mixed Steam reviews at 64%, so newcomers may get frustrated.

C3B1V55CDL0C:party.text: A free platform fighter where up to eight can brawl on one console, knocking each other off the stage with weapons and legends. It's quick to start and works for a big group like yours.
C3B1V55CDL0C:party.caveat: It has lots of characters and moves to learn, so beginners can lose badly to anyone who has played before.

9P9FTXPKQ35P:party.text: The newest in the football series you already like, with up to four players on one console. You can jump straight into matches with friends, which is a natural fit for a group that plays FIFA.
9P9FTXPKQ35P:party.caveat: It's another annual FC release, so if you already play FC 25 the local play may feel much the same, and it's limited to 4.

BVCRSR6XSDW5:party.text: Motorbike racing with physics-based stunts and tracks, with up to four competing on one console. The ragdoll crashes are funny, and it has a track editor like the build-your-own-level feel of Ultimate Chicken Horse.
BVCRSR6XSDW5:party.caveat: The tracks are tagged as difficult, and the head-to-head multiplayer is limited to 4, so it may not suit a casual crowd.

BRJNRZ9N734V:party.text: Full-contact demolition racing where you ram, spin out and wreck friends' cars around the track. The crashes are physics-driven and funny, and a race needs no tutorial, which suits a chaotic couch session.
BRJNRZ9N734V:party.caveat: The listed local play is flagged as a conflict in the data, so check that split-screen or shared-console versus actually works with your group size before planning a night around it.

9PKZRN4RJRC9:party.text: Up to four gladiators are chained together and fight in an arena, using chains and surroundings to beat enemies. The forced togetherness is the kind of chaos found in Gang Beasts and Knight Squad 2, with adjustable difficulty.
9PKZRN4RJRC9:party.caveat: It's a difficult roguelike with combat-heavy runs, so it asks for more commitment than a quick party game, and it's limited to 4.

9PDGC1Z6ZHTP:party.text: A throwback to the classic arcade-style hockey game, with up to four on one console. It's easy to pick up, fast, and competitive, which fits the sports-game side of your group.
9PDGC1Z6ZHTP:party.caveat: It's deliberately retro in graphics and controls, so it may feel dated, and it's capped at 4.

9PPKR9N31BW6:party.text: A fast competitive platformer where up to four race and use items to knock each other behind. It's a chaotic, quick-round game in the same spirit as Boomerang Fu.
9PPKR9N31BW6:party.caveat: The player count is disputed in the data and little is known about its reception, and fast platforming can be hard for casual players.

C3SQQG5Q6Z64:party.text: Arcade racing with short tracks, loops, and jumps, with split-screen for up to four. It's easy to learn and each race is quick, so a group can pass the controller around.
C3SQQG5Q6Z64:party.caveat: It's about chasing perfect times and tagged as difficult, so it may feel less chaotic or funny than the games you like.

C4B8XR1LCXR5:party.text: An aerial combat game with split-screen co-op for up to four, in a pulp-adventure alternate 1930s. It's an old Xbox 360 title, so it's more of a novelty than a modern party game.
C4B8XR1LCXR5:party.caveat: It's an older game with dated controls and a flight-combat learning curve, and it's not a quick-learn party pick.

9PJGM0T0827V:party.text: An off-road racer with four-player split-screen across gravel, ice, snow and sand. It suits a group that likes the competitive side of FIFA, with a livery editor and adjustable difficulty to help mixed skill levels.
9PJGM0T0827V:party.caveat: It's a fairly serious racer rather than a chaotic party game, and the Steam reviews are mixed, so it may feel less funny than your usual picks.

9NVD16NP4J8T:party.text: American football with up to four players on one console, for a group that already likes sports games like FIFA. You can play head-to-head or team up against the computer.
9NVD16NP4J8T:party.caveat: It has a lot of rules and play-calling to learn, so it's not quick for non-fans, and it's capped at 4.

9PC1KTWW5PB5:party.text: Up to four can share one console for hockey, which suits the FIFA-style sports nights. Two teams on the couch pass, shoot and check each other, with a simulation feel that rewards a bit of practice.
9PC1KTWW5PB5:party.caveat: The simulation controls are deeper than your usual quick-to-learn party picks, so newcomers may struggle at first.

9PJRQHMCFQGS:party.text: Up to four take turns rolling balls down the lane, so it works as a low-pressure couch game for groups who like sports. Everyone can follow what is happening quickly, and the competition is about score.
9PJRQHMCFQGS:party.caveat: It is a realistic bowling simulation played in turns, so it lacks the chaos and slapstick of Gang Beasts or Boomerang Fu.

C2P985H1H42H:party.text: A classic four-player minigame party game with a sci-fi setting and more than 45 minigames across six arenas. Short rounds are easy to pick up, which fits the quick, funny, competitive nights you like.
C2P985H1H42H:party.caveat: It is an old Xbox 360-era title, so visuals and minigame quality may feel dated, and it caps at four players.

9N79TQTZTQQ4:party.text: A pixel-art beat 'em up where up to four pick from 15 Marvel heroes and brawl through levels together. It is close to the co-op fighting of Minecraft Dungeons and Knight Squad 2, with easy-to-learn controls.
9N79TQTZTQQ4:party.caveat: It is co-op against enemies rather than versus chaos, and the main run is short, so it may be a one-evening game.

9PB3GGBSG27C:party.text: Up to four share a console for hockey, covering the same couch-sports ground as FIFA. Teams of friends can play against each other, and the adjustable difficulty helps mixed skill levels.
9PB3GGBSG27C:party.caveat: It is a simulation with many controls, so non-hockey fans may take a while to enjoy it.

9N8CD0XZKLP4:dan.text: A direct step from Ori and the Blind Forest: you platform through a large interconnected map, unlocking movement abilities that open new routes, with light environmental puzzles along the way. The combat is more fluid and the exploration loop is close to Hollow Knight's.
9N8CD0XZKLP4:dan.caveat: The story leans heavily on emotional beats, and the boss chases can be frustrating if you want slower, more deliberate platforming.

9N116V0599HB:dan.text: You explore a large, interconnected world of hand-drawn ruins, unlocking movement abilities that open new routes, with tough platforming and boss fights in the vein of Hollow Knight. It leans on the same atmospheric, map-reading exploration you value.
9N116V0599HB:dan.caveat: It is reputedly very demanding, with no adjustable difficulty, so some bosses and long runs back after dying could be frustrating.

BRKMHZX1RCF2:dan.text: You sail a ship around a Caribbean open world, boarding vessels, diving for wrecks and climbing through jungle and port towns as a pirate-turned-assassin. It offers the historical exploration and stealth you enjoy in other Assassin's Creed games.
BRKMHZX1RCF2:dan.caveat: Its collectibles and side activities are plentiful and can feel repetitive, and some tailing missions are restrictive.

9MT5NJ5W7B8Z:dan.text: You roam an open-world Hogwarts and its surrounding lands, casting spells in combat and solving small environmental puzzles while uncovering collectibles. The atmospheric exploration is the main tie to what you like.
9MT5NJ5W7B8Z:dan.caveat: It is combat-heavy with a large checklist of map activities, which can feel like the grind you tend to avoid.

9N4W31HSMVVD:dan.text: You live as a peasant-turned-knight in a detailed 15th-century Bohemia, exploring, talking your way through quests and fighting with realistic swordplay. The historical immersion may appeal if you like Assassin's Creed's period settings.
9N4W31HSMVVD:dan.caveat: It is slow, simulation-heavy and difficult, with a lot of time needed for its systems and combat to feel comfortable.

9PDDP6ML6XHF:dan.text: You build a medieval village from scratch while hunting, gathering, crafting, and managing seasons and resources. The base building and survival loop resemble Minecraft, with some management on top.
9PDDP6ML6XHF:dan.caveat: It involves repetitive gathering and long build-up periods, which may feel grindy, and the RPG and combat parts are fairly basic.

9P4LSLG7B8CT:dan.text: This is a fast, acrobatic metroidvania in which you unlock time powers, trace map routes and fight bosses. It has the platforming and ability-gated exploration of Hollow Knight and Ori, with adjustable difficulty if the combat gets rough.
9P4LSLG7B8CT:dan.caveat: Combat is more fast-paced and flashy than Hollow Knight's, and the world feels more guided and less mysterious.

9NLRT31Z4RWM:dan.text: You explore an isometric world as a small fox, finding hidden paths and piecing together a cryptic in-game manual to uncover secrets. The discovery-driven puzzling and exploration suit your liking for deep puzzles.
9NLRT31Z4RWM:dan.caveat: Its combat is fairly punishing and the intentionally opaque design can leave you unsure where to go next.

9NXQKPGMHH9G:dan.text: An older first-person RPG set in underground caverns, where you explore, solve puzzles, and cast spells by drawing runes with the mouse or controller. The puzzle and exploration focus overlaps with your tastes.
9NXQKPGMHH9G:dan.caveat: It is an early-2000s game with dated controls and interface, and it has some horror elements, which you generally avoid.

9NQGN8TGNT8P:dan.text: You plan routes across a desolate landscape, carrying cargo over rough terrain and balancing weight and stamina. The slow, solitary exploration and survival logistics echo some of what you enjoy in Subnautica.
9NQGN8TGNT8P:dan.caveat: Much of the game is walking and delivering, plus a long, heavily cinematic story, which may feel slow or repetitive.

BX3JNK07Z6QK:dan.text: You explore a sprawling wasteland, crafting gear, making choices that change quests and surviving in a hostile desert. It rewards curiosity and wandering in the way your open-world favorites do.
BX3JNK07Z6QK:dan.caveat: It is an older, rough-edged game with dated combat and a heavy focus on dialogue and shooting rather than puzzles.

9NXWKGRHT31F:dan.text: Dropped onto an open-world island, you explore, scavenge and hunt for crafting upgrades, and clear enemy outposts either stealthily or loudly. The outpost-liberating, map-revealing loop echoes Assassin's Creed, and the island setting adds some survival-exploration flavor.
9NXWKGRHT31F:dan.caveat: It is a combat-heavy shooter with a lot of gunplay and no adjustable difficulty, so it's much less about puzzles or quiet discovery than Subnautica or Hollow Knight.

9PCR3Z2MSM4T:dan.text: A roguelike where you fight through procedurally arranged rooms, choosing boons and upgrades each run while the story progresses through repeated attempts. The hand-drawn art and tight combat are similar to Hollow Knight's polish.
9PCR3Z2MSM4T:dan.caveat: The run-based structure with meta-progression can feel grindy, which you tend to avoid.

C5HHPG1TXDNG:dan.text: You jump through the strange mental worlds of different characters, solving platforming and environmental challenges with psychic powers. It pairs the platforming of Celeste and Ori with inventive, story-driven level design.
C5HHPG1TXDNG:dan.caveat: It is an older platformer with sometimes loose controls and camera, and it is lighter on deep puzzles than you may want.

BQ1W1T1FC14W:dan.text: You wander a huge snowy fantasy world, picking up quests, exploring dungeons and building your own character as you go. It suits the self-directed, atmospheric exploration you enjoy.
BQ1W1T1FC14W:dan.caveat: It is a very long game with simple combat and few real puzzles, and it is easy to sink huge amounts of time into it.

9N7P8GVMF6SS:dan.text: You solve first-person logic puzzles with tools like beams, boxes and connectors while exploring a mysterious sci-fi world. It gives you the deep puzzles you like, with a philosophical story woven in.
9N7P8GVMF6SS:dan.caveat: Its story has a lot of dialogue and reading, and some later puzzles may be hard enough to stall you.

9NSFGM8J6MBJ:dan.text: You build vehicles from blocks, such as cars, boats, and aircraft, and use them to complete challenges in an open world. The engineering and tinkering have some of the same satisfaction as Infinifactory.
9NSFGM8J6MBJ:dan.caveat: The challenges are secondary to the building, and it is geared toward multiplayer, so solo play may feel thin.

9PGMNX4HG2C7:dan.text: You play as Ezio in Rome, climbing the city, assassinating targets and rebuilding districts while recruiting your own assassins. It is a classic entry in the series you already enjoy for its historical settings and stealth.
9PGMNX4HG2C7:dan.caveat: It is built closely on Assassin's Creed II, so it can feel familiar, and its optional activities can pile up.

BW9TWC8L4JCS:dan.text: A big open-world Assassin's Creed set in ancient Greece, with exploration by land and sea, stealth assassinations, and dialogue choices that shape the story. It's a natural fit for someone who enjoys most of the series.
BW9TWC8L4JCS:dan.caveat: It's long and leans on RPG-style leveling and side content, which can feel grindy if you try to clear the map.

9NBLGGH43KZB:dan.text: You explore colorful planets, dig terrain with a deformation tool, gather resources and build bases, with automation among its systems. It combines Subnautica-style exploration with Minecraft-like building and crafting.
9NBLGGH43KZB:dan.caveat: Resource gathering and travel can feel grindy, and it is lighter on challenge and depth than Oxygen Not Included or other factory games.

BZ6W9LRPC26W:dan.text: You explore one shifting, interconnected building, unlocking powers like telekinesis and levitation that open previously blocked areas. That backtracking-with-new-abilities loop resembles a metroidvania, and the odd, atmospheric setting suits a player who likes exploring.
BZ6W9LRPC26W:dan.caveat: Combat is a large share of the play and is mostly gunplay and power-throwing, with no difficulty adjustment, and it has some horror-leaning moments.

C5F2XDQPPJKZ:dan.text: You plan stealth assassinations across open, layered city districts, using teleport-style and supernatural powers to find routes and solve how to reach each target. The mission-based infiltration has some of the same observation and planning appeal as Assassin's Creed.
C5F2XDQPPJKZ:dan.caveat: It is a stealth-action game with some combat rather than a deep puzzle game, and the story is short on its own.

C3KLDKZBHNCZ:dan.text: You scavenge a ruined wasteland and build up settlements with crafted structures and supply lines, which touches on his survival and base-building tastes. Exploration is open and self-directed, similar in spirit to Assassin's Creed.
C3KLDKZBHNCZ:dan.caveat: Looting, crafting and gunfights can turn grindy over a 100+ hour full playthrough, and the settlement building is shallow next to real factory games.

C0KJ40T9QD86:dan.text: You roam a large open Himalayan map, clearing outposts and moving by gyrocopter or elephant. It follows the same tower-and-outpost exploration structure as Assassin's Creed, and stealth is a viable approach.
C0KJ40T9QD86:dan.caveat: It is mainly a shooter with repeating outpost loops, and it has little of the puzzle, crafting or systems depth he usually prefers.

BV6BRSLFJW3W:dan.text: You hunt, craft gear and tame animals in a Stone Age open world, which brings survival and crafting elements to a Far Cry structure. Exploring a prehistoric map has some of the same pull as Assassin's Creed settings.
BV6BRSLFJW3W:dan.caveat: Underneath is the usual Far Cry loop of outposts and combat, and the crafting and village upgrades can feel like light grinding.

9NF5S7MLM8XT:dan.text: You explore a small open city as a cat, climbing, jumping and nudging objects around to reach new areas and trade items for progress. The gated-area exploration echoes a light metroidvania, in a short, relaxed form.
9NF5S7MLM8XT:dan.caveat: It's low-stakes and gentle, so it lacks the challenge and depth of Ori or Rain World.

9NX6K9HN4F4K:dan.text: You play an artist in a 16th-century Bavarian village, investigating murders by talking to townsfolk, piecing together clues and making choices that change later events. It's closer to a deduction-driven mystery than a puzzle game, with distinctive illuminated-manuscript art.
9NX6K9HN4F4K:dan.caveat: It's dialogue-heavy with little mechanical challenge, which may feel slow if you want hands-on puzzles.

9NBLHDB0WLHZ:dan.text: This is a hand-drawn, non-violent platformer where you play a violin and platform your way through to restore a musical world. The art and atmosphere echo Ori, and the short length means little time commitment.
9NBLHDB0WLHZ:dan.caveat: It is tagged difficult, and it is a linear platformer without the map-driven exploration of Hollow Knight.

C5K89TFLSV19:dan.text: You pick a direction and explore a huge open fantasy world at your own pace, with dungeons, guilds and magic to try. The self-directed wandering has some of the same appeal as Assassin's Creed.
C5K89TFLSV19:dan.caveat: It is a dated RPG with stiff combat and a lot of time-consuming side content, so the full experience takes a very long time.

C40860J5R2MP:dan.text: A third-person survival horror game where you scavenge ammo and crafting parts, sneak around enemies and explore semi-open hub areas. Resource management and exploration are the main hooks.
C40860J5R2MP:dan.caveat: It's explicitly horror with heavy combat and gore, which you generally avoid.

9P8XK6X57GBF:dan.text: An action-adventure set in early 20th-century America and Japan, following a fifty-year story with open-world exploration. The historical setting may appeal to your Assassin's Creed side.
9P8XK6X57GBF:dan.caveat: It's a brawler from the Yakuza team with PvP tags, so puzzles are likely a minor part.

9P1S707BPW6W:dan.text: You play a teenager investigating her parents' disappearance, turning sketches into evidence and solving logic puzzles to uncover the mystery. It combines exploration, detective work and deduction.
9P1S707BPW6W:dan.caveat: It's new with little review data, and it's story-led, so the puzzles may be light.

9NRQVQ7ZRM7Z:dan.text: You fight in a mix of real-time action and pausable tactical commands across a story-driven journey through Midgar. If he enjoys character-driven narratives like The Alters, the emotional story could carry him.
9NRQVQ7ZRM7Z:dan.caveat: It is heavily linear and combat-focused, with little exploration or puzzle depth, and it only covers the first part of the original story.

9P743P6195Q5:dan.text: You work through themed escape rooms, hunting for clues and combining objects to crack mechanical and logic puzzles. It suits the observational, solve-it-yourself side of Monument Valley, and it can be played solo with no online competition.
9P743P6195Q5:dan.caveat: Rooms are short, self-contained puzzles, so it lacks the deep, systemic puzzle design of Opus Magnum or Infinifactory and is built mainly around co-op play.

9PMN4DGRT1LN:dan.text: An open-world fantasy action RPG where you fight with style-weaving combat, choose your reputation and can buy property and run shops. It's lighter and funnier than a typical serious RPG.
9PMN4DGRT1LN:dan.caveat: It's mostly combat and choices with little puzzle depth, and the data on this one is thin.

9NW6JK0ZC9J6:dan.text: A city-builder where you manage an island nation's economy, resources and politics across eras. It has the production-planning side of Oxygen Not Included but with satire.
9NW6JK0ZC9J6:dan.caveat: It's more about managing politics and budgets than designing systems, so it's less puzzle-like than your factory games.

9NFW93G1GFXG:dan.text: A difficult action RPG with souls-like combat that rewards learning enemy patterns. If you like Cuphead's pattern-learning challenge, it has something similar in a different form.
9NFW93G1GFXG:dan.caveat: It's a combat-focused souls-like with no difficulty adjustment, and there's little here for puzzles or exploration.

9NL8MF491NRZ:dan.text: A 5v5 online football game with character roles and skills. It's built around team matches.
9NL8MF491NRZ:dan.caveat: It's a competitive multiplayer sports game with no overlap with your tastes.

9N40DK5N4LD4:dan.text: A turn-based RPG where you investigate murders tied to a TV world, fighting in dungeons and building bonds with friends. The mystery plot is the draw.
9N40DK5N4LD4:dan.caveat: It's a very long, dialogue-heavy JRPG with a school-life calendar, which may feel like a time sink.

9P4NV23Q6QC2:online.text: You and your friends play scientists stuck in an underground research facility, scavenging, crafting and building a base while fighting off paranormal creatures. It's a cooperative survival game with a team-based, resource-gathering loop similar to Deep Rock Galactic.
9P4NV23Q6QC2:online.caveat: It's a long survival-crafting game, so it works best if your group will keep playing together over many sessions.

9NKV34XDW014:online.text: You and friends catch creatures, build a base, automate chores and explore an open world together. Shooting and crafting are there if you want them, but there's no competitive ladder, so it suits a relaxed group on headsets.
9NKV34XDW014:online.caveat: Progress is grindy, and the critic score is mixed compared with the very positive player reviews.

9P7L9H478GGV:online.text: A fast, old-school sci-fi shooter where you blast through Strogg-infested levels. It has co-op support, so you can play it with friends, though it's mostly a classic campaign.
9P7L9H478GGV:online.caveat: It's a retro, single-player-first campaign, so co-op is a side feature and not the focus.

BPKDQSSFQ9WV:online.text: A cover-based third-person shooter campaign you can play in online co-op, with a squad fighting through sci-fi enemies. Horde-style modes also suit a team that likes working together.
BPKDQSSFQ9WV:online.caveat: It's an Xbox 360-era game, and the online player base may be small.

BXBJQ1932138:online.text: You and friends track animals across large open maps, then take careful shots. It's slow and low-pressure, with plenty of room to chat on headsets while walking and spotting.
BXBJQ1932138:online.caveat: It's very slow and has no real combat intensity, so it suits chatting more than excitement.

9NSFGM8J6MBJ:online.text: You build vehicles from parts, such as cars, boats and planes, then take them out together to explore and tackle challenges. It's a creative, low-pressure online co-op game that suits laughing about each other's builds.
9NSFGM8J6MBJ:online.caveat: There's no shooting, and the building tools take time to learn before they feel fun.

9N431PX143P8:online.text: An open-world driving game where you can cruise, explore Japan and do events with friends online. It's relaxed and easy to drop in and out of, with no ladder you have to climb.
9N431PX143P8:online.caveat: It's driving-focused, with none of the shooting or building that Dan's regular games have.

BQVQTL3PCH05:online.text: You explore planets, mine resources, craft gear and build bases, with the option to team up online. It shares the gather-and-build loop of Deep Rock Galactic but at a much slower, more relaxed pace.
BQVQTL3PCH05:online.caveat: It's mostly about solo-style exploration and long grinds, so it's less focused on shooting alongside friends.

9NKX70BBCDRN:online.text: An open-world racing game where you can drive around Mexico and do events with friends online. Difficulty is adjustable, and there's no pressure to compete seriously.
9NKX70BBCDRN:online.caveat: It's all driving, so it won't scratch the shooting and building itch of Dan's usual games.

BRZHFR5XBLQS:online.text: You grind rails and bounce around an open-world city while shooting mutants with silly weapons. It's colorful and jokey, with an energetic, arcade feel closer to Fortnite's mobility than most shooters.
BRZHFR5XBLQS:online.caveat: The campaign is mainly a solo experience, so it may not give your group much to do together.

9NQMVR9WL9FW:online.text: You crew a train that travels between strange worlds, gathering materials, crafting weapons and fighting creatures with up to four players. Building and upgrading the train together gives a squad a shared project, similar to Deep Rock's teamwork.
9NQMVR9WL9FW:online.caveat: Reception is more mixed than the other survival picks, so expect rough edges.

9PLCL2VB2SC0:online.text: A co-op zombie shooter where you and friends hold positions and fight off huge hordes together, with class-based roles that reward teamwork on headsets, similar to Deep Rock Galactic's swarm fights.
9PLCL2VB2SC0:online.caveat: Levels get repetitive, and it's less polished than Deep Rock Galactic.

9NKHKBQJSSC3:online.text: You fight as a robot gladiator in a voxel arena, slicing up enemies with a sword, and co-op lets a friend join. It's funny and chaotic, with more silly physics than competitive tension.
9NKHKBQJSSC3:online.caveat: The combat is melee-focused and can be hard, and co-op is less central than the solo campaign.

9P8XKV2D5DZ5:online.text: Dig for resources underground, then rush back to defend your dome from alien waves. The mining loop resembles Deep Rock's, though it's a small-scale pixel-art game.
9P8XKV2D5DZ5:online.caveat: It's mainly a solo experience, so it's less suited to a group on headsets.

9PDDP6ML6XHF:online.text: Hunt, build a village and manage seasons with co-op available, so friends can share the work of survival. It's a slow, settle-in game that rewards chatting while you craft.
9PDDP6ML6XHF:online.caveat: The pace is slow and management-heavy, with little action compared with Fortnite or Deep Rock.

9NBLGGH43KZB:online.text: You and friends land on colorful planets, dig terrain, gather resources and craft gear and bases. It's gentle co-op exploration with no pressure, similar to Deep Rock Galactic's mining but calmer.
9NBLGGH43KZB:online.caveat: There's little combat, so it may feel slow if you want action.

C3QH42WRGM3R:online.text: Beyond the campaign, this has co-op and multiplayer modes, so you could team up on headsets with friends for some shooting. The same sci-fi, combat-heavy shooting as Deep Rock Galactic, but faster and more aggressive.
C3QH42WRGM3R:online.caveat: It is mainly a fast, difficult single-player shooter with no adjustable difficulty, and its competitive multiplayer may feel sweatier than the casual co-op Dan prefers.

9PJ6FV3130QZ:online.text: An open-world survival game on a desert planet where you gather resources, build a base and explore with friends online. The sci-fi setting and shared building and crafting loop overlap with what you play already.
9PJ6FV3130QZ:online.caveat: It's a big time commitment with MMO-style systems, and some PvP elements may not suit a casual group.

9MT8PTGVHX2P:online.text: Six Halo games, with campaigns playable in online co-op, so you can fight through the story with a friend on headsets. The shooting is accessible and has a clear sense of progression.
9MT8PTGVHX2P:online.caveat: Multiplayer here can be competitive, and it's a big collection that takes time to get into.

C4DMGRPNSHXG:online.text: A hacking-focused open-world action game set in Chicago, where you use the city's systems to fight and sneak. It has some online features, but it's mainly a solo story.
C4DMGRPNSHXG:online.caveat: It's mostly a single-player campaign, so it doesn't offer much for a group on headsets.

C0KJ40T9QD86:online.text: An open-world shooter in the Himalayas with vehicles, outposts and a co-op option. You can explore and cause chaos together, which fits a casual group.
C0KJ40T9QD86:online.caveat: Co-op is limited and the story is mostly solo, so it works better as an occasional side activity.

BR7X7MVBBQKM:online.text: You liberate a rural county from a cult in an open-world shooter, with full 2-player co-op. It suits a pair of friends who want to roam, fish and fight together.
BR7X7MVBBQKM:online.caveat: Co-op is limited to two players, so it won't work for a bigger group.

C1SDBNRFXT1D:online.text: A cover-based sci-fi shooter with online co-op, so Dan's group can work through the campaign together. It is straightforward, with clear objectives and a team feel, from the same studio behind Fortnite.
C1SDBNRFXT1D:online.caveat: It's an older game, with a short campaign and likely thin matchmaking.

BPRPQSKXTD1L:online.text: A real-time strategy game set in the Halo universe, with online co-op available. You build bases and command units, which is a calmer way to play with friends.
BPRPQSKXTD1L:online.caveat: It's a strategy game designed for controllers, so it's a very different style from Dan's shooters.

9PNRSC0J6DT8:online.text: You drive heavy off-road trucks through mud and snow with friends, winching each other out and planning routes together. It's a relaxed sandbox where cooperation matters more than skill.
9PNRSC0J6DT8:online.caveat: It's slow and methodical, with no shooting, so it can be frustrating or dull for some groups.

C2N9CS4FS1QR:online.text: A tactical open-world shooter where you and up to three friends take down a drug cartel in Bolivia. Planning approaches and talking over headsets is the whole appeal.
C2N9CS4FS1QR:online.caveat: The missions repeat across a very large map, and the critic reception was mixed.

9PD5BM2Z8C4L:online.text: You move around while your weapons fire automatically, surviving waves of monsters and building up powerful upgrades. It's relaxed and easy to pick up.
9PD5BM2Z8C4L:online.caveat: The co-op is local only, so playing with friends online won't work.

BSXLFN5QQZSC:online.text: A jokey hacker adventure in San Francisco where you take over cameras and drones, and can drop into co-op to cause chaos with friends. It's a relaxed, sandbox-style game that suits casual headset sessions.
BSXLFN5QQZSC:online.caveat: It's mainly a single-player story, and the co-op is a smaller side feature than the main game.

BRJNRZ9N734V:online.text: Wreckfest is a demolition-derby-style racer where you smash through packs of cars on tracks and in derby arenas. Its crashy, slapstick physics suit a casual voice-chat session with friends, and it has co-op tagged, so you can mess around together without ladder pressure.
BRJNRZ9N734V:online.caveat: Racing is the core of it, so if the group wants cooperative play like Deep Rock Galactic, you'll mostly be competing against each other.

BRKMHZX1RCF2:online.text: A pirate adventure where you sail the Caribbean, board ships and explore islands. It's one of the easier open-world games to enjoy at a relaxed pace.
BRKMHZX1RCF2:online.caveat: It's a single-player story game, so it doesn't offer anything to do with friends online.

9PBG4MTM3JJC:online.text: One to four players drop onto alien planets, build and defend a base, then extract with what they've collected. It's the closest match here to Deep Rock Galactic's squad-based loop of mining, defending, and escaping.
9PBG4MTM3JJC:online.caveat: It's an early Game Preview, so expect missing content and rough edges.

9NL8MF491NRZ:online.text: A 5v5 online football game where players take on different roles and skills. Team play on headsets fits Dan's usual setup, and the arcade style leans toward fun over simulation.
9NL8MF491NRZ:online.caveat: It's all competitive matches against other teams, with no real co-op, so it may feel sweatier than Dan's usual play.

9NK039GWVTVC:online.text: A lightweight online RPG where you team up with friends to clear dungeons, defeat monsters, and collect loot to craft better gear. The low pressure and loot-driven loop suit casual co-op sessions.
9NK039GWVTVC:online.caveat: It's an early Game Preview with little track record, so content may be thin.

9P743P6195Q5:online.text: You and a friend share a voice call while working through themed puzzle rooms together, passing clues back and forth and cracking codes under a time limit. It's cooperative with no opponents, so the pressure is mild and the talking is the point.
9P743P6195Q5:online.caveat: It's a puzzle game rather than an action game, so it may suit a one-off evening better than the regular sessions Fortnite or Deep Rock Galactic give you.

9NFW93G1GFXG:online.text: A fantasy action RPG with online co-op, where you fight tough enemies alongside a friend. It's more cooperative than competitive, and it fits the combat-heavy side of your tastes.
9NFW93G1GFXG:online.caveat: Souls-like games are difficult and punishing, so it could be frustrating for a casual group.

9NS86BQ33SPX:taylor.text: A relaxed open world where you take odd jobs, try mini games and follow silly story missions at your own pace. Exploring a bright, funny sandbox is low-pressure and easy to play in short sessions.
9NS86BQ33SPX:taylor.caveat: It's a physics-based goofy sandbox, not a mystery or magic story, so the plot is light.

9NSF0BGH8D86:taylor.text: A cozy fantasy life-sim where you restore a valley, befriend Disney characters and follow gentle story quests. It suits Tay's Stardew Valley enthusiasm and is easy to play an hour at a time.
9NSF0BGH8D86:taylor.caveat: The story is sweet rather than mysterious, and the loop of gathering and crafting can feel repetitive.

BQ1W1T1FC14W:taylor.text: A huge fantasy world to explore at your own pace, with spell-casting, ruins, and a main story plus many side quests. It echoes what you liked in Hogwarts Legacy: wandering, finding secrets and collectibles, and playing in short sessions.
BQ1W1T1FC14W:taylor.caveat: The world is very large with many quests running at once, which is what made Assassin's Creed Odyssey hard to keep track of, and combat can get bloody with no difficulty options mentioned.

9P20JCF7BV93:taylor.text: A short, classic fantasy quest in a pixel-art style. You explore, build a party of magic users and fighters, and play turn-based battles with no frantic action, so it suits a relaxed hour at a time.
9P20JCF7BV93:taylor.caveat: The story is very simple and light on mystery or clue-solving, so it may feel thin next to the story-driven games you like.

9NWDPFPPK30V:taylor.text: A turn-based fantasy adventure with a crystal-and-magic quest and a job system for changing your party's roles. Battles are calm and paced by menus, and it's easy to play in one-hour sessions.
9NWDPFPPK30V:taylor.caveat: The plot is basic and there's no mystery to solve, and older-style dungeons and random battles can feel repetitive.

C2WKJJ9F5936:taylor.text: A fantasy open world where you wander Albion, explore dungeons and taverns, and use magic alongside a story-led quest line. The exploring and spell use echo Hogwarts Legacy, and the pace is easy to play in hour-long sessions.
C2WKJJ9F5936:taylor.caveat: Combat is real-time with melee and ranged attacks as well as magic, it has no difficulty setting, and the game is a 2008 title with dated controls and visuals.

9N8C07SS8C9D:taylor.text: A classic fantasy tale told through turn-based battles, with magic, a clear next destination and a emotional story. Combat is menu-based, so there's no frantic reflex play and you can go at your own pace.
9N8C07SS8C9D:taylor.caveat: It's a fairly linear, old-school RPG with no mystery-solving, and it has no difficulty setting.

9N9C8SV0S16W:taylor.text: A turn-based fantasy adventure built around magic and a job system where you choose and swap character classes. Battles are menu-driven rather than frantic, and the story is lighter in tone than some of the series.
9N9C8SV0S16W:taylor.caveat: The story is less of a mystery and more of a straight quest, and the class system can take some time to get your head around.

9N255K81XBD3:taylor.text: A turn-based fantasy with a big ensemble cast, magic and a dramatic, emotional story. Battles are menu-driven rather than frantic, so you can play in short sessions and take your time with each fight.
9N255K81XBD3:taylor.caveat: The plot is more character drama than puzzle or whodunit, and there is no difficulty setting.

9N8FQ28Z6QX3:taylor.text: A first-person 1937 adventure where you follow a historical mystery across the globe, solving puzzles, exploring and finding clues. It has adjustable difficulty, and the story is the main draw, much like the history and secrets you enjoyed in Mirage.
9N8FQ28Z6QX3:taylor.caveat: It includes stealth and some fistfights, which can get tense, and the combat is a more physical, hands-on style than spell casting.

9NZDHXL9SJJ8:taylor.text: A long, story-heavy RPG where you balance school life with turn-based dungeon battles, and a mystery about hidden targets runs through it. It's funny and stylish, and has adjustable difficulty, which suits an hour at a time.
9NZDHXL9SJJ8:taylor.caveat: It's very long and the calendar system can feel pressured, and the dungeons are stylised fantasy combat rather than detective work.

9P86LLDCL5CC:taylor.text: A relaxing island life-sim where you farm, fish, craft and explore a forest at your own pace. It's close to Tay's solo Stardew Valley favorite and well suited to hour-long sessions.
9P86LLDCL5CC:taylor.caveat: It has little mystery or plot, and the amount to do can feel overwhelming, as Odyssey did.

9MZG3KH0PVZC:taylor.text: The third Ezio game follows an assassin through Constantinople, with historical settings and a story-led plot. It's a good way to see more of the series if Mirage and Odyssey worked for you.
9MZG3KH0PVZC:taylor.caveat: Combat and stealth are central, with some violence, and it has no difficulty setting; the map and its side activities can also feel crowded.

9NV01PJJLXN2:taylor.text: A historical Assassin's Creed set in the 18th century, with sailing, exploring and a story that flips the usual assassin viewpoint. You follow a story-led path with collectibles, which fits your liking for secrets.
9NV01PJJLXN2:taylor.caveat: It's another large Assassin's Creed with lots of map content to track, which was the issue in Odyssey, and the combat is violent.

9NH019ZFFHTV:taylor.text: A calm simulation where you diagnose problems in cars, take parts apart and put them back together like a puzzle. It has adjustable difficulty and no pressure.
9NH019ZFFHTV:taylor.caveat: It has no story or mystery, so it only appeals if Tay enjoys the mechanical puzzle-solving itself.

9NTRS771L8HL:taylor.text: A detective RPG in which you investigate a murder by interrogating suspects, searching a district for clues and choosing what to say. It's almost all reading and conversation, with no real-time combat.
9NTRS771L8HL:taylor.caveat: The text is dense, which may be more than you want, and the tone is dark and political, with mature themes.

9PDC8J1BSV8B:taylor.text: A relaxed driving game where you deliver packages around a mountain town and slowly uncover its strange secrets and residents. It's short and gentle, with a hint of mystery.
9PDC8J1BSV8B:taylor.caveat: It is only about five hours, which is much shorter than the long games Tay enjoys.

9N36BLQF3FX6:taylor.text: A funny, colorful puzzle-mystery where you talk your way through puppet-filled scenes and weird gods to stop the world ending. The detective work, story focus and puzzle solving fit your taste for twisty, light-hearted mysteries.
9N36BLQF3FX6:taylor.caveat: It has no difficulty options, and the quirky, cartoony tone is closer to Spiritfarer's whimsy than to a historical whodunit.

9PKJTP6DTND3:taylor.text: A turn-based RPG mixing magic and cyberpunk, with a story-driven plot about a murder case. You talk to characters, make plans and fight in tactical battles.
9PKJTP6DTND3:taylor.caveat: The tactical combat can be tough and a bit grim, and the sci-fi setting is far from Tay's usual cozy fantasy.

BXVCFBJBNS17:taylor.text: A vast open-world fantasy where you create your own character and explore a strange land of magic at your own pace. It's long, with lots of lore, which suits Tay's patient approach.
BXVCFBJBNS17:taylor.caveat: It's an old game with dated combat and menus, and little to point you toward objectives.

9PGMNX4HG2C7:taylor.text: Ezio's story continues in Renaissance Rome, with historical settings, a story-led plot and a city to explore. It suits you if you enjoyed Mirage and Odyssey's history.
9PGMNX4HG2C7:taylor.caveat: Combat and stealth involve violence, there is no difficulty setting, and the open city has many side activities that can pull you away from the main thread.

BQ9Q620NC614:taylor.text: A fairy-tale adventure with watercolor art, where a girl explores a magical world and fights in gentle turn-based battles. It's a moderate length with a story told in verse, so it's easy to follow.
BQ9Q620NC614:taylor.caveat: The story is simple, with little mystery or solving, and at about 12 hours it's shorter than Tay prefers.

9NKBDN695GTT:taylor.text: You play first-person escape rooms: examine objects, move furniture, find hidden details and crack locks. It's very close to your liking for escape-room puzzles, and it's easy to play in short sessions with no combat.
9NKBDN695GTT:taylor.caveat: It's mostly puzzle rooms with light story, so it won't give you the long narrative of a whodunit, and there's no difficulty setting.

9NF5S7MLM8XT:taylor.text: A cozy, funny game where you play a cat exploring a city, knocking things over and meeting characters. It's a gentle open world with easy-going exploration.
9NF5S7MLM8XT:taylor.caveat: It's only a few hours long and has very little story or mystery.

9NX6K9HN4F4K:taylor.text: A historical murder mystery in 16th-century Bavaria, where you talk to villagers, collect clues and decide who to accuse. It combines Tay's interest in history and detective work, with no combat.
9NX6K9HN4F4K:taylor.caveat: There is a fair amount of reading, and the story is serious, so it's less cozy than some of Tay's other picks.

BR74RLMH966K:taylor.text: A short, gentle turn-based RPG where you trick-or-treat through a neighborhood, solve small quests and swap costumes for different battle powers. The tone is funny and cozy, and the battles are simple enough to play at a relaxed pace.
BR74RLMH966K:taylor.caveat: It is only about five or six hours and light on story depth and mystery, so it may feel slight next to Hogwarts Legacy.

9NNKJNRKFT0G:taylor.text: A third-person fantasy action game that blends magic with physics, where you take on huge creatures. The magic and colourful world have something in common with Hogwarts Legacy.
9NNKJNRKFT0G:taylor.caveat: The fights against giant creatures are real-time and can be demanding, and there is no difficulty setting.

C042M8GWKS34:taylor.text: You play a tiny stacking doll who hops into larger dolls and uses each one's special ability to solve puzzles in a charming, vintage-era world. There's no combat, and you can often find several ways to solve each puzzle.
C042M8GWKS34:taylor.caveat: It's short at around six hours and quirky rather than a deep mystery.

9P2J5D12GJL5:taylor.text: A huge open-world fantasy RPG where you can follow the main quest or wander off into guild quests, dungeons and magic. If you enjoyed exploring Hogwarts Legacy at your own pace, the long, unhurried format is similar.
9P2J5D12GJL5:taylor.caveat: It's an older game with dated visuals and clunky real-time combat, there are no difficulty options, and the world has no clear objective markers to keep track of.

9P1S707BPW6W:taylor.text: A mystery in which you play a teenager investigating her parents' disappearance, turning sketches into evidence and solving logic puzzles while exploring. It's story-led and focused on spotting clues, much like a puzzle-driven whodunit.
9P1S707BPW6W:taylor.caveat: It's a newer, little-known game, and the tone is emotional and gets darker as the case develops.

9PMN4DGRT1LN:taylor.text: A fairytale-style open-world action RPG with humor, magic, spell and sword combat, and a village you can shop and settle in. Its storybook fantasy tone is close to what you enjoyed in Hogwarts Legacy.
9PMN4DGRT1LN:taylor.caveat: Combat is real-time and there are no difficulty options, and the story seems to lean on choices more than on mystery.

9NRQVQ7ZRM7Z:taylor.text: A fantasy sci-fi story set in the city of Midgar, with magic and characters who drive the plot. It's a well-regarded, story-led game if you're willing to take on the combat.
9NRQVQ7ZRM7Z:taylor.caveat: Combat is a big part of it and is fast and intense, which you've said you don't want, and there's no difficulty setting.

9N40DK5N4LD4:taylor.text: A turn-based RPG with a murder mystery at its core: you investigate strange deaths in a small town, with a team of friends and a long story. Turn-based fights suit a non-frantic pace.
9N40DK5N4LD4:taylor.caveat: The story is dark in places and has some supernatural horror, and time-management and social systems add a lot to keep track of.

9P743P6195Q5:taylor.text: You solve escape-room style puzzle rooms in a school setting while uncovering a long-buried conspiracy, which suits your love of locks, hidden details and clue-driven mysteries. It plays solo or co-op, and rooms are self-contained, so short sessions work.
9P743P6195Q5:taylor.caveat: It has no adjustable difficulty setting, and timed rooms (the bell) may feel pressured compared with the unhurried pace you like.

C22T53SQ7FLM:couch.text: A collection of 30 older Rare games, including platformers and puzzle games, which you can dip into for short sessions. Some of the lighter titles might suit your platforming and puzzle tastes.
C22T53SQ7FLM:couch.caveat: Many of the games are old, combat-heavy or shooters, and only some support co-op, so you'll have to pick carefully.

9N3LGKGF3CC2:dan.text: A hand-drawn 2D metroidvania where you explore a ruined alien-built land and fight bosses with Sekiro-style parry-and-deflect combat. The map-driven exploration and precise boss duels echo Hollow Knight and Ori, with a sci-fi twist on the setting.
9N3LGKGF3CC2:dan.caveat: Combat is built around tight parrying and is tagged difficult with no adjustable difficulty, so the boss fights could frustrate if you prefer exploration over duels.

9PMVJR05PFJW:dan.text: An open-world Paris you move through by climbing rooftops and sneaking past Nazi patrols, with sabotage targets to scout and take out. That infiltration and exploration loop echoes Assassin's Creed, in a 1940s occupied-city setting.
9PMVJR05PFJW:dan.caveat: It leans on gunplay and driving combat more than pure stealth, and it's an older game with dated controls and mission structure.

9MW4MFG0192L:dan.text: A platforming-and-exploration game where you descend through crypts, caverns and ruins as a scrappy goblin, with some survival pressure. The atmospheric, dark-fantasy descent has some kinship with Hollow Knight's world, though it's far more comedic.
9MW4MFG0192L:dan.caveat: It's early access and built around co-op with friends, so solo play may feel thinner, and the horror elements and chaotic tone may not suit someone who prefers precise, deep design.

9MW4MFG0192L:online.text: You and up to three friends crawl through crypts and caverns as goblins, working together on a headset much like a Deep Rock Galactic run. It's co-op exploration with a survival edge and no ladder to climb.
9MW4MFG0192L:online.caveat: It's in early access, so content and polish may be thin, and the horror and platforming can get frustrating without adjustable difficulty.

BV83SM3191S5:couch.text: A fantasy adventure where one player controls a young elf who can transform into different elemental creatures, with a second player joining in. The family-friendly tone and creature-swapping puzzles suit a two-person couch session.
BV83SM3191S5:couch.caveat: It is combat heavy, and the older controls and no adjustable difficulty could frustrate Tay if fights get tough.

C3L4J3H7H12R:online.text: Dead Island 2 supports online co-op, so you and your friends can team up on headsets to smash through zombie-filled Los Angeles. The jokey tone and crafting-based weapon upgrades keep it relaxed, closer to Deep Rock Galactic's teamwork than to Fortnite's competition.
C3L4J3H7H12R:online.caveat: It is a gory, combat-heavy horror game with no adjustable difficulty, and its repetitive missions may wear thin over a long group session.

9P8S1MN4066K:taylor.text: A pixel-remastered fantasy RPG with a story-focused plot and magic spells. You explore towns and dungeons and talk to characters at a turn-based pace. At about 10 hours, it's a short, easy-to-pace way to get the story-and-magic feel of Hogwarts Legacy.
9P8S1MN4066K:taylor.caveat: It's an older, linear turn-based RPG with no mystery or puzzle solving, and it has no difficulty options, so it may feel thin next to the detective games Tay prefers.

BRJNRZ9N734V:couch.text: A crash-heavy racing game where you ram, spin out and wreck cars on dirt tracks and demolition arenas. The physics-driven carnage is funny, and the damage is the point rather than winning cleanly, which suits a relaxed session together.
BRJNRZ9N734V:couch.caveat: The listed local play is versus only, not co-op, and racing against each other at speed may feel competitive and skill-driven for Tay.

BX03760D0QGN:couch.text: You build a custom character, explore a hub city and take on story missions in the Dragon Ball universe. The two-player local mode is versus fighting, and the customization and adventure side has a little of Stardew's progression.
BX03760D0QGN:couch.caveat: It's grindy, combat-heavy and online-focused, with local play limited to head-to-head fighting, so it's a poor match for Tay's dislike of high-skill games and for cooperative play on one TV.

9N6639H7VGH4:party.text: Classic four-player split-screen shooter where you run around Bond-themed maps trying to out-shoot each other. It's easy to pick up and gives a different kind of chaos from your brawlers and platformers.
9N6639H7VGH4:party.caveat: It tops out at 4 players and is a dated, serious shooter. Your 5 to 8 person nights won't fit, and it's less slapstick than your usual picks.

9N36BLQF3FX6:dan.text: You solve puzzles by sucking up and launching dialogue among quarrelling gods and puppets, with detective-style clue gathering in a fantasy world. The mystery and puzzle focus echoes Monument Valley and Chants of Sennaar.
9N36BLQF3FX6:dan.caveat: It's a dialogue-driven, story-heavy puzzler, so it may feel light on the deep mechanical puzzles you like in Opus Magnum.

9P8XJRLCLH2P:dan.text: You run a shop by day and delve into randomized dungeons by night, hauling back loot to sell and crafting better gear. The exploration and roguelike loop is close to Don't Starve and Ball x Pit.
9P8XJRLCLH2P:dan.caveat: The dungeon runs are combat-heavy and the loot-and-sell cycle can feel repetitive, which may read as grindy.

BRJNRZ9N734V:dan.text: This is a demolition-style racing game with detailed car damage physics, where you race and crash through derbies and tracks. It has little in common with your usual puzzle, survival or metroidvania picks.
BRJNRZ9N734V:dan.caveat: It's a vehicle racing game focused on crashes and competition, and the exploration and atmosphere tags don't reflect much of what you actually do.

9N21ZCV0JW6V:dan.text: You ride a horse around an open park, exploring and unlocking areas in a light adventure. The open-world exploration is the only real overlap with Assassin's Creed.
9N21ZCV0JW6V:dan.caveat: It's a family-friendly game aimed at younger players, so the depth and challenge are likely well below what you enjoy.

9P0NPLQ9P1DB:dan.text: You patrol a town on foot, handling fines, reports and incidents, with a Casual Mode for a more relaxed pace. It's a methodical, observational job with some detective-style work.
9P0NPLQ9P1DB:dan.caveat: The routine of patrol tasks is repetitive and low on puzzles or story, and it's still in early access.

9P81K2C8RBF4:dan.text: This is a top-down shooter where you fight enemies, collect loot and customize characters, solo or in co-op. It leans on action and loot rather than puzzles or exploration.
9P81K2C8RBF4:dan.caveat: Its multiple endgame systems and loot chasing are built around grinding, which you tend to avoid.

9PHTX5QZ035T:dan.text: This is a first-person shooter set in a survival-horror setting, where you scavenge to craft weapons on an eerie island. The crafting and exploration gives it a slight link to survival games.
9PHTX5QZ035T:dan.caveat: It's fast, combat-heavy and horror-driven, which is a poor match for your puzzle and exploration tastes.

9NBZ7Z3JRXQ8:dan.text: You fight fires as part of a squad, managing equipment and tactics in a simulation. It has some of the procedural, systems-handling feel of simulations, but little of the planning depth of factory games.
9NBZ7Z3JRXQ8:dan.caveat: It's mainly a co-op action simulation and may lack the puzzle or optimization depth you like.

9N6639H7VGH4:dan.text: This is a remake of a classic first-person shooter with stealth-or-force missions as Bond. It's a straightforward combat game with split-screen multiplayer.
9N6639H7VGH4:dan.caveat: It's a shooter at heart and has little of the puzzle, exploration or systems depth you tend to prefer.

9ND3HTTQ0GKB:dan.text: You play a mouse restoring a burrow, gathering resources, crafting, baking and knitting through a cozy winter. It's a gentle survival loop that fits fans of Don't Starve and Subnautica who want something calmer.
9ND3HTTQ0GKB:dan.caveat: It's low on challenge and puzzle depth, so the crafting loop may feel too gentle.

9P81K2C8RBF4:online.text: A top-down shooter and looter with up to 4-player online co-op. You shoot enemies, collect loot and customize characters together, which is close to the squad-based, combat-heavy loop of Deep Rock Galactic from a different angle.
9P81K2C8RBF4:online.caveat: It's a loot-and-RPG grind with a story, so it's more about gear and builds than the moment-to-moment teamwork and mining of Deep Rock.

9P0NPLQ9P1DB:online.text: You patrol a town as a police officer, handling small incidents and exploring the streets, with online co-op available. It has a Casual Mode, so friends can wander and chat without pressure.
9P0NPLQ9P1DB:online.caveat: The work is slow and procedural, and it's tagged early access, so it may not hold a group that wants action like Fortnite or Deep Rock.

9NBZ7Z3JRXQ8:online.text: You join a firefighting squad and respond to fire alerts, with online co-op for working as a team. Splitting up roles over headsets is a natural fit for friends who like cooperative play.
9NBZ7Z3JRXQ8:online.caveat: It's a fairly methodical simulation with little fast action, and I don't have much detail on how varied the missions get over time.

9NRHQLZX3900:online.text: You play a pigeon in a spy-comedy setting, tracking and dealing with anomalies around a city, with online co-op. The jokey tone and low stakes fit a relaxed headset session with friends.
9NRHQLZX3900:online.caveat: The humor is the main draw, so it may wear thin after a few sessions if the missions get repetitive.

9P0NPLQ9P1DB:taylor.text: You patrol a town on foot, spotting issues and dealing with them, and the Casual Mode is a relaxed way to play. It leans on observation and exploration, with no frantic combat or gore.
9P0NPLQ9P1DB:taylor.caveat: It's a procedural job sim rather than a story-driven mystery, so there's little plot, and it's still in early access.

9N21ZCV0JW6V:taylor.text: You ride a horse around an open park, exploring and unlocking new areas, which echoes the pleasure of roaming Hogwarts. It's family-friendly, so there's no gore or horror.
9N21ZCV0JW6V:taylor.caveat: It's a racing and exploration game aimed at younger players, with no mystery or deep story, and it has no difficulty options.

BRJNRZ9N734V:taylor.text: A demolition-derby racer where you crash cars around tracks, with a funny, chaotic feel. Mostly it's about driving skill and physics rather than anything you've said you enjoy.
BRJNRZ9N734V:taylor.caveat: It's fast, loud, full-contact racing with no story or mystery, which is the frantic style you tend to avoid.

9NRHQLZX3900:taylor.text: You play a pigeon working for a secret agency, tracking down strange anomalies across a city in a silly conspiracy-flavored adventure. The humor may appeal, and you can play it co-op.
9NRHQLZX3900:taylor.caveat: It's an action-leaning comedy sim with little mystery depth, and the anomaly-hunting may get repetitive.

9N3P3TRJGWV0:couch.text: A kid-friendly open-world platformer where two players explore Dino Island together in split-screen, completing rescue missions and playing minigames. The light exploration and simple platforming sit close to the LEGO games they enjoy.
9N3P3TRJGWV0:couch.caveat: It's aimed at young children, so the puzzles and challenge are likely very light and may feel repetitive.

9NWWL1CBWFCG:dan.text: You place buildings by day and defend your little kingdom against waves at night, a compact blend of base building and tight resource decisions. The minimalist, rule-driven loop echoes the optimizing side of Ball x Pit and Oxygen Not Included.
9NWWL1CBWFCG:dan.caveat: It's a small-scale action-strategy game with repeating waves, so it lacks the deep puzzle or exploration structure you usually favor.

9NRBW3FJSJWT:dan.text: A relaxed open-world platformer where you deliver packages as a tanuki postman and explore the area to repair a shrine. The exploration and light platforming overlap with Ori, though at a much gentler pace.
9NRBW3FJSJWT:dan.caveat: It's cozy and low-stakes, so it likely won't offer the challenge or depth of Celeste or Hollow Knight.

9N3P3TRJGWV0:dan.text: A light platforming and exploration game on a dinosaur island with simple missions and minigames. It's built for local co-op play with others.
9N3P3TRJGWV0:dan.caveat: It's aimed at young children, so it offers little of the depth or challenge you tend to look for.

9N74KFV7253H:dan.text: A town-building sandbox where you move into a village, help locals, and build things to make the place thrive. The light management loop is the closest link to your sim and builder tastes.
9N74KFV7253H:dan.caveat: It's a gentle, family-oriented life sim, with little of the systems depth of Oxygen Not Included or Infinifactory.

9N8RS7CW8CGL:dan.text: A cheerful adventure where you explore lands, gather materials, craft, and solve small puzzles to revive a kingdom. The crafting and exploration are the parts most relevant to you.
9N8RS7CW8CGL:dan.caveat: It's a light, kid-friendly game, so puzzles and combat are likely shallow compared with what you usually play.

9MTGCZ84M503:dan.text: A four-player co-op shooter where you fight hordes of monsters, with adjustable difficulty. It's the most action-focused pick here and plays well as a team game.
9MTGCZ84M503:dan.caveat: It's a combat-heavy horror shooter built around co-op, with no puzzles or exploration, and it's best played with friends rather than solo.

9WZDNCRFHV60:dan.text: A straightforward sudoku collection with daily challenges, several difficulty levels, and variants like Irregular and Ice Breaker. It's a simple logic puzzle you can pick up for a few minutes.
9WZDNCRFHV60:dan.caveat: It's classic number logic rather than the inventive, systems-driven puzzles of Opus Magnum or Monument Valley.

9MTGCZ84M503:online.text: Four-player online co-op shooter where you and friends on headsets fight through monster hordes. The shooter-and-horde combat is close to what you do in Deep Rock Galactic, and difficulty is adjustable, so you can keep it relaxed.
9MTGCZ84M503:online.caveat: It's more of a straight action shooter than DRG's mining and class-teamwork, so it may feel less varied over longer sessions.

9N8RKWJT32L4:online.text: You and up to three friends play a crew of firefighters, tackling fires and rescues together. It's cooperative and low-pressure compared with Fortnite, and it suits voice chat since you'd coordinate who does what.
9N8RKWJT32L4:online.caveat: It's a simulation with no adjustable difficulty and no critic or player scores in the data, so it's hard to know how polished or varied it is.

9NRBW3FJSJWT:taylor.text: You play a lazy tanuki delivering packages around a small open area, meeting locals and gradually restoring a run-down shrine before a summer festival. The cozy exploring and light town-helping echo the gentle pace of Stardew Valley.
9NRBW3FJSJWT:taylor.caveat: It's a light, cute platformer with no mystery or deep story to dig into, and no difficulty options are listed, so it may feel too slight for a player who wants clues and history.

9P4NV23Q6QC2:dan.text: You explore a sprawling underground research facility, scavenging and crafting gear, building a base, and solving environmental problems as you go. The survival-exploration loop and sci-fi setting echo Subnautica, with plenty of discovery to chew on.
9P4NV23Q6QC2:dan.caveat: Combat is a large part of the experience and it's built around co-op, so solo play may feel tougher and more fight-heavy than you'd like.

C2CSDTSCBZ0C:dan.text: You traverse interconnected planets, gaining Force abilities that open previously blocked routes, with some environmental puzzles along the way. The backtracking structure will feel familiar from metroidvanias like Hollow Knight.
C2CSDTSCBZ0C:dan.caveat: Combat is a souls-like lightsaber duelling system with a real difficulty bar, and it's a 3D action game rather than a 2D one.

9N3P3TRJGWV0:taylor.text: A kid-friendly open-world platformer where you roam Dino Island, exploring, completing missions and customizing looks. It's gentle, with no gore or horror, so the pace is calm and easy to play in short sessions.
9N3P3TRJGWV0:taylor.caveat: It's aimed at young children, so it offers little mystery, clue-solving or story depth, and it has no adjustable difficulty.
